This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a question that a studio asks before a launch. Then it explains
the idea behind it. It ends with a **Do it** task and one set of questions.
Every question on this page has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary market-share fragmentation cross-platform test-device sideloading app-store reliable-source comparison-criteria >}}

## 8.1 Players and devices

- **Market share** worldwide: about **7 in 10** phones run Android, about
  **3 in 10** iOS. It differs by country: check it, with its date.
- Android: many makers, cheap to expensive phones, many versions
  (**fragmentation**).
- iOS: one maker, few models, most on a recent iOS; players often spend
  more on games.

![Players and devices.](images/reach-devices.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
One worldwide number does not fit every country.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The phones at home"}
Count the Android phones and the iPhones in your family. Is the share near
70 / 30? Why might it be different?

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "5 Android phones and 1 iPhone: about 80 / 20.
Five people is a small group, and prices and shops in our country are not
the same as in the whole world."

- ☐ You wrote two counts and the share.
- ☐ You gave a reason: a small group, or a country that differs from the world.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Players and devices"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="one in ten|Apple and Google"}
About how many phones in ten run Android worldwide?
:   about seven

    Why: Worldwide, about 7 in 10 phones run Android and 3 in 10 run iOS.

Who makes iPhones?
:   only Apple

    Why: iOS runs only on Apple's own phones.

What does fragmentation mean for a tester?
:   many models and versions to test

    Why: Android runs on many makers, screens, chips and versions.

Why look at the share of one country?
:   players differ from country to country

    Why: In one country iPhones may be common, in another budget Android phones.
:::
:::

## 8.2 Building and testing

- **Android:** Android Studio on Windows, macOS or Linux; several real
  **test devices** (weak, typical, strong).
- **iOS:** Xcode only on a **Mac**; an older and a newer iPhone.
- **Unity** is a **cross-platform** engine: one project, both builds. For
  iOS a Mac finishes the build.
- Byte Bay has five Windows PCs and no Mac: Android today, iOS only with a
  Mac.

![Tools and test phones.](images/build-test.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/launch-planner.html" poster="sims/launch-planner.png" title="Launch Planner: Android, iOS or both?" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Virtual phones on the PC do not replace real phones: they do not heat up and
have no real battery.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Plan the launch"}
In **Launch Planner**, choose "Android and iOS" and "only Windows PCs".
What problem do you see? How many test phones are needed?

::: {.check}
The planner says: "an iOS build needs a Mac with Xcode", so Byte Bay must
buy or rent a Mac first. The launch on both needs at least 5 test phones:
3 Android phones (weak, typical, strong) and 2 iPhones (an older and a
newer one).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Build and test"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="any PC|a phone"}
On which computer can Xcode run?
:   only a Mac

    Why: Xcode runs only on macOS.

Byte Bay has only Windows PCs. Which build can it make?
:   Android

    Why: Android builds are made on any PC; iOS needs a Mac.

How many test phones does a launch on both need (in the planner)?
:   5

    Why: 3 Android phones (weak, typical, strong) and 2 iPhones.

What makes Unity a cross-platform engine?
:   one project gives both builds

    Why: Unity builds the same game for Android and for iOS.
:::
:::

## 8.3 Open or closed: installing and updates

- **Android: open.** Google Play, other stores or an `.apk`
  (**sideloading**); makers change the system; updates from each maker,
  late or never.
- **iOS: closed.** The **App Store** (other stores only in some regions);
  only Apple changes it; updates for all supported iPhones at once.
- A tester tests old Android versions too.

![Openness and updates.](images/openness.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Open is not always unsafe, closed is not always safe: update and install
from known sources.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Where can apps come from?"}
Android: search Settings for "Install unknown apps". Which apps may install
other apps? Do not turn anything on. iPhone: is there a way to install an
app from a file?

::: {.check}
On Android, "Install unknown apps" lists apps such as the browser or the
file manager, each with "Not allowed": sideloading is possible, but off
until you allow it. On an iPhone there is no such setting: apps come from
the App Store (other stores only in some regions). Leave the setting off.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Open or closed?"}
Android or iOS? You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="both|neither"}
Installs an `.apk` file from outside the store.
:   Android

    Why: Android allows sideloading from a file.

Updates every supported phone at the same time.
:   iOS

    Why: Apple updates all supported iPhones at once.

Phone makers change the system.
:   Android

    Why: Each maker changes Android for its own phones.

Only one company changes the system.
:   iOS

    Why: Only Apple changes iOS.
:::
:::

## 8.4 Facts you can trust: reliable sources

- **Criteria:** the points you compare, chosen for the decision: reach,
  tools, test devices, installing, updates.
- **Reliable source:** a known author or organisation, a **date**, its
  data. Best for a platform fact: the **maker's official page**.
- Weak: forum posts without a date, pages that sell something, old blogs.
- The share in Rami's country: a market report from last month → use it,
  with the month.

![Criteria and sources.](images/criteria-sources.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/source-check.html" poster="sims/source-check.png" title="Source Check: can you trust this source?" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The first search result is often an advertisement or an old page.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Judge five sources"}
Judge all five sources in **Source Check**. Which three signs did you use?

::: {.check}
Use sources 1, 3 and 5: Apple's page about Xcode and Google's page about
testing (the makers' own pages, dated) and the market report (dated, with
its data). Skip source 2 (a forum post without author or date) and source 4
(an old shop page that sells something). The three signs: a known author or
organisation, a date, and its data.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Sources"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the first search result|any blog"}
Which source is best for the fact "Xcode runs only on a Mac"?
:   Apple's developer page, with this year's date

    Why: The maker's own page is the best source about its own tool.

A forum post has no author and no date. Do you use it?
:   no, find a better source

    Why: Without author and date you cannot check it.

A page sells phone cases. Is it a reliable source?
:   no, it sells something

    Why: A page that sells something is an advertisement.

A market report shows its data and its date. Do you use it?
:   yes, with its date

    Why: A share changes, so the date goes into the table.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Platform Pick {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The producer of **Byte Bay** asks six questions before the launch of
*Pocket Quest*. The studio has **only Windows PCs**. The questions are about
the build, the reach, the testing, a **source for the share in Jordan**, an
old **Android 11** bug, and installing **from a file**.

{{< sim file="sims/platform-pick.html" poster="sims/platform-pick.png" title="Platform Pick: Android or iOS for the launch?" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The producer's questions"}
Byte Bay has only Windows PCs. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="iOS|the iPhone has no bugs"}
Which platform can Byte Bay build this week?
:   Android

    Why: An iOS build needs a Mac with Xcode.

Why does Android need more test phones?
:   many makers, screens, chips and versions

    Why: That is fragmentation; iOS has a few models.

Which source fits the share of Android phones in Jordan?
:   a market report with its data and the month

    Why: A share changes, so it needs a dated source with data.

Why test on Android 11?
:   many phones never get the newest version

    Why: Android updates come from each maker, late or never.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Advice (harder)"}
Choose the best first launch for each studio.

::: {.match extra="iOS only, today|no launch"}
A small studio with only Windows PCs, and players with budget phones.
:   Android first

    Why: It builds on any PC, and its players have Android phones.

A studio with a Mac, whose players mostly have iPhones.
:   iOS first, or both

    Why: The Mac makes the iOS build possible, and the players are on iOS.

A studio with a Mac, and players all over the world.
:   both platforms

    Why: Both together reach almost every phone.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Android reaches about 7 in 10 phones worldwide, iOS about 3 in 10: check
  your country, with a date.
- Android builds on any PC; iOS needs a Mac. Android needs more test
  phones (fragmentation).
- Android is open and updated by each maker; iOS is closed and updated by
  Apple for all iPhones.
- A fact goes into a comparison only with a reliable source: an author, a
  date and its data.
